The International Society of Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH) is an international organization whose medical criteria play a foundational role in the Danish healthcare system's quality monitoring of anticoagulation therapy. Within the context of the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and its annual reports on [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation), the ISTH's guidelines are utilized to standardize the definition and measurement of bleeding complications [^src2]. 

Specifically, the society's criteria are adapted to define [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (major bleeding) for [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], a key quality indicator that tracks the incidence of severe bleeding events among prevalent atrial fibrillation patients [^src1]. This adaptation ensures that the measurement of bleeding risks—including severe events such as [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]] (intracranial bleeding)—is internationally standardized, allowing for consistent evaluation of treatment safety across national, regional, and local levels in Denmark [^src2]. The indicator's definition is explicitly tied to these adapted ISTH criteria in the program's methodology [^src3].

While Indikator 7 does not have a predefined numerical standard or target threshold, it relies entirely on these adapted ISTH criteria to accurately report bleeding incidence [^src1]. The methodological framework of the RKKP reports details how these criteria are operationalized using specific diagnosis codes (ICD-10-DK) and registry data from the Danish National Patient Register, making the ISTH's definitions a critical technical reference for clinical quality measurement in the Danish healthcare system [^src4].
